findings.title: Tenant/actor/event boilerplate triad (org(), currentUserId(), emit()) copy-pasted across financial-crime & audit services
findings.cvss: Maintainability risk: a change to event/tenant/actor resolution (e.g. a new DomainEvent field, a fix to the SecurityContext principal cast) must be hand-applied in 13+ services; drift between copies is near-certain and already visible (ShariaService/RrpService/FraudService/OpResService carry byte-identical helpers while ScmService diverged into a different org() that defaults to 1L).
findings.description: The same three private helpers — `static Long org() { return TenantContext.requireOrganisationId(); }`, `static Long currentUserId() { ... instanceof GrcUserDetails ... }`, and `void emit(String trigger, String entityType, Long entityId, String correlationId, Map payload) { publisher.publishEvent(new DomainEvent(...)); }` — are duplicated verbatim across ShariaService, RrpService, FraudService and OpResService (and at least 9 other modules platform-wide per the grep for `private static Long org() { return TenantContext.requireOrganisationId(); }`, which hits 13 files, and the `if (auth == null || !auth.isAuthenticated()` cast which hits 17 files). jscpd independently flags the `emit/currentUserId` block as a clone, e.g. FraudService:381 <-> OpResService:292 <-> AiLifecycleService:349 (19 lines) and ShariaService:672 <-> ObService:625 (32 lines).
findings.rootCause: No shared base class or helper component for the cross-cutting concerns every event-emitting service needs (tenant id, acting user, DomainEvent publish). Each module's author copied the previous module's service.
findings.evidence: grep `private static Long org() { return TenantContext.requireOrganisationId(); }` => 13 files. grep `if (auth == null || !auth.isAuthenticated()` => 17 files. jscpd clones: fraud/service/FraudService.java:381 <-> opres/service/OpResService.java:292 (19 lines); sharia/service/ShariaService.java:672 <-> openbanking/service/ObService.java:625 (32 lines); cpty/service/CptyService.java:528 <-> rrp/service/RrpService.java:592 (30 lines).
findings.impact: High change-amplification cost; correctness divergence already present (ScmService.orgId() silently substitutes tenant 1L while the others throw — see QUAL-FA-007). A single security-relevant fix to currentUserId() would need 13 edits.
findings.reproduction: Open ShariaService.java (682-699), RrpService.java (600-617), FraudService.java (384-400), OpResService.java (295-311) side by side; the org()/currentUserId()/emit() bodies are character-identical.
findings.resolution: Extract a `protected abstract` base class (e.g. `EventEmittingService`) or a `@Component DomainEventPublisher` plus a `SecurityHelper.currentUserId()` and `TenantContext.requireOrganisationId()` wrapper, and have these services delegate. Removes ~17 LOC * 13 services of duplication and forces a single definition of actor resolution.

findings.title: Per-entity DTO mappers and *_ALLOWED transition tables duplicated wholesale across sister services
findings.cvss: Each new column on an entity requires touching both the entity, the request-apply block, AND the hand-written builder mapper; the builder-chain mappers are long, near-mechanical, and structurally identical between modules, so they are a steady source of 'forgot to map field X' defects.
findings.description: Every service hand-rolls `private static XResponse toX(XEntity)` builder chains (RrpService has 5, ShariaService has 6, FraudService 3, OpResService 3) that mechanically copy 15-30 getters into a builder. The same pattern of static transition maps (`RESOLUTION_ALLOWED`, `FINDING_ALLOWED`, `NC_ALLOWED`, `PRODUCT_ALLOWED` in ShariaService; `ALLOWED` in Rrp/Fraud/OpRes/Finding/IaEngagement/SanctionsHit) plus an identical `guardTransition` body is repeated. jscpd flags the mapper region directly (RiskControlFindingPivotService:622 <-> :638; CptyService:528 <-> RrpService:592, 30 lines).
findings.rootCause: Project convention is hand-written builder mappers (no MapStruct) and a private transition-map-per-service. Both are valid choices individually, but the verbatim repetition is unmanaged.
findings.evidence: RrpService 5 mappers (lines 621-712, ~92 LOC of pure builder chains). ShariaService 6 mappers (701-819, ~119 LOC). ShariaService declares 4 separate `Map<String,Set<String>>` ALLOWED tables (78-105). The guardTransition body in FraudService:350-356 and OpResService:274-280 is identical apart from the message prefix.
findings.impact: Field-mapping omissions are silent (a forgotten `.fieldX()` compiles fine and just returns null to the UI). High line-count with low information density inflates every service file.
findings.reproduction: Compare RrpService.toOption (652-666) with the entity setters in addOption (220-241): both enumerate the same 14 fields; adding a 15th requires editing both.
findings.resolution: Adopt MapStruct (or a shared reflective copy like the BeanUtils approach ScmService already uses) for response mapping, and factor the transition-guard into a tiny generic helper `StateMachine.guard(map, from, to, label)` reused by all services.

findings.title: Dead dashboard query: FraudService counts status="TRIAGE" which the state machine never assigns
findings.cvss: Functional-correctness smell rather than crash: the `triageCount` tile on the Fraud dashboard is hard-wired to always read 0 because no case is ever persisted with status TRIAGE, yet the field is presented to users as a live count.
findings.description: `dashboard()` populates `.triageCount(caseRepo.countByOrganisationIdAndStatus(orgId, "TRIAGE"))`. The class-level comment (lines 71-76) and the ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS map (77-84) explicitly state TRIAGE is NOT a held state — `triage()` (151-183) sets `triagedAt` and immediately advances to INVESTIGATING or FALSE_POSITIVE. No code path ever calls `setStatus("TRIAGE")`. Therefore this count is permanently 0 and is dead/misleading.
findings.rootCause: Dashboard was written against an earlier design where TRIAGE was a held state; when the team collapsed TRIAGE into a transient decision step (documented in the NOTE comment) the dashboard query was not removed.
findings.evidence: grep '"TRIAGE"' in module/fraud => single hit at FraudService.java:333 (the dashboard). ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS has no TRIAGE key on either side; createCase sets status DETECTED, triage() sets INVESTIGATING/FALSE_POSITIVE.
findings.impact: Users see a 'Triage' tile permanently stuck at 0, implying no cases are in triage when in fact cases pass through it instantly. Wastes a DB count round-trip every dashboard load.
findings.reproduction: Create a fraud case, call triage(); query `dashboard().triageCount` — it returns 0 regardless of how many cases were triaged.
findings.resolution: Either remove the triageCount tile, or repurpose it to count cases with `triagedAt != null && status == 'INVESTIGATING'` (i.e. currently-in-investigation-post-triage). Removing is cleaner given the documented design.

findings.title: Unreachable guard branch in RrpService.transitionCycle for SUBMITTED
findings.cvss: Logic-correctness smell: the defensive `if (Set.of("SUBMITTED").contains(to))` block can never be entered because the ALLOWED map upstream already rejects any transition whose target is SUBMITTED, so the bespoke 'use the /submit endpoint' message is dead and an actual SUBMITTED attempt yields the generic 'Illegal transition' message instead.
findings.description: `transitionCycle` first computes `allowed = ALLOWED.getOrDefault(from, Set.of())` and throws if `!allowed.contains(to)` (144-148). The ALLOWED map (71-78) never lists SUBMITTED as a reachable target from any state. So by the time control reaches line 149 `if (Set.of("SUBMITTED").contains(to))`, `to` cannot be SUBMITTED — the branch is unreachable and its informative message ('Use the dedicated /submit endpoint to lodge with SAMA') is never shown.
findings.rootCause: The author added a friendly redirect for SUBMITTED but placed it after the generic allow-list check that already short-circuits the same case.
findings.evidence: ALLOWED map values: DRAFT->{IN_PREPARATION}, IN_PREPARATION->{BOARD_REVIEW}, BOARD_REVIEW->{APPROVED,IN_PREPARATION}, APPROVED->{IN_PREPARATION}, SUBMITTED->{ACKNOWLEDGED}, ACKNOWLEDGED->{CLOSED}, CLOSED->{}. No value set contains SUBMITTED.
findings.impact: Misleading dead code; an operator who POSTs a SUBMITTED transition gets the generic error instead of the intended hint to use /submit. Minor, but the branch will confuse future maintainers reasoning about reachability.
findings.reproduction: Call transitionCycle with toStatus=SUBMITTED on an APPROVED cycle: it throws 'Illegal transition APPROVED → SUBMITTED' from line 146, never reaching the friendlier message at 150.
findings.resolution: Move the SUBMITTED hint ahead of the allow-list check, or delete it and document /submit in the controller. Preferred: hoist the special-case before the generic guard.

findings.title: RiskControlFindingPivotService swallows all RuntimeExceptions silently via safeList/safeOpt across 8 foreign-module repositories
findings.cvss: Reliability/observability risk: every cross-module repository call is wrapped in a catch-all that returns an empty list/Optional with no log, so a genuine DB/mapping failure in any of the 8 source modules degrades the pivot to 'no linked controls/findings/CAPA' indistinguishably from a legitimately empty graph — silently producing wrong analytics with no trace.
findings.description: `safeList(Supplier<List>)` and `safeOpt(Supplier<Optional>)` catch `RuntimeException` and return `List.of()` / `Optional.empty()` with no logging. They wrap ~15 call sites spanning RiskRepository, ControlRepository, RiskControlLinkRepository, ControlAssessmentRepository, FindingRepository, two CapaTaskRepositories, ControlTestDefinitionRepository and ControlTestRunRepository. Any exception (lazy-init, mapping error, constraint, NPE) is absorbed and the pivot reports an empty section. The `dataCompletenessPct` metric then reads as a data-quality gap rather than an error.
findings.rootCause: Defensive 'graceful missing-link handling' (documented in the class Javadoc) was implemented as a blanket catch-all rather than as null/empty handling on the actual finder return values.
findings.evidence: Lines 656-663: `catch (RuntimeException ex) { return Collections.emptyList(); }` — no log. Lines 665-668: `catch (RuntimeException ex) { return Optional.empty(); }` — no log. The only logged catch in the class is emitPivotEvent (516-518). parseControlCodes (425-430) likewise catches Exception and silently falls back.
findings.impact: A real failure in any source module is invisible: the pivot returns a misleadingly-empty graph, undermining the analytics the module exists to provide, and leaving no log breadcrumb for triage.
findings.reproduction: Inject a repository that throws (e.g. simulate a mapping error in ccmRunRepo.findRecentForTest): ccmCoverageForControls returns zero-coverage stats with no warning logged; the pivot looks healthy.
findings.resolution: At minimum log at WARN with the supplier context inside safeList/safeOpt (the class already has an Slf4j logger). Better: catch only the specific 'not visible to tenant' case and let infrastructure exceptions propagate to the controller's 500 handler.
references: Effective Java Item 77: Don't ignore exceptions

findings.title: Governance pivot/3LoD services reach directly into 8+ other modules' repositories (cross-module layering violation)
findings.cvss: Coupling/architecture risk: the governance module's services depend at compile time on the internal repositories and entities of risk, controls, audit_lc, capa, ccm, iam, policy, privacy_lc — so any schema/finder change in those modules can break governance, and the modular-monolith boundary the project documents (one repository layer per module) is bypassed.
findings.description: RiskControlFindingPivotService injects RiskRepository, ControlRepository, RiskControlLinkRepository, ControlAssessmentRepository, FindingRepository, two CapaTaskRepository beans (capa + audit_lc), ControlTestDefinitionRepository and ControlTestRunRepository — 9 repositories owned by 6 other modules — and queries their entities directly. ThreeLinesService similarly injects RiskRepository, FindingRepository, CapaTaskRepository, PolicyDocumentRepository, DsrCaseRepository and UserRepository. Both also import foreign entities (Risk, Control, Finding, CapaTask, PolicyDocument, User...). This is heavier coupling than the documented per-module repository pattern.
findings.rootCause: The aggregation/dashboard services need cross-module data and the codebase exposes no module-level read API (query service / facade), so they bind directly to foreign repositories. The pivot class Javadoc even acknowledges 'owns no tables' and reaches into source repos.
findings.evidence: RiskControlFindingPivotService constructor (106-130) takes 9 repositories from risk/platform.controls/audit_lc/capa/ccm. ThreeLinesService fields (97-105) take 6 repositories from risk/audit_lc/capa/policy/privacy_lc/iam. jscpd also flags governance/pivot importing across modules indirectly. The CCM coverage method even pages 100 runs per definition in a loop (351-379) — N+1 over a foreign repo.
findings.impact: Tight compile-time coupling: a finder rename in any of 6 modules forces a governance edit; the modular boundary is not enforceable; foreign N+1 query patterns (ccmRunRepo in a per-definition loop) live outside the owning module's control.
findings.reproduction: Inspect imports of both services: each imports entity + repository types from 6+ sibling modules under com.tss.grc.module.*.
findings.resolution: Introduce read-only query facades per source module (e.g. RiskQueryService.openRisksForOrg(orgId), CcmQueryService.coverageForControls(...)) and have governance depend on those interfaces instead of foreign repositories. This restores the one-repository-layer-per-module boundary and lets each module own its query/N+1 strategy.
references: CLAUDE.md: 'repository/ Spring Data JPA — org-scoped' per module

findings.title: ScmService.orgId() silently defaults to tenant 1L on null context, diverging from the require-or-throw convention used everywhere else
findings.cvss: Tenant-safety/consistency smell: when TenantContext is empty (e.g. a misconfigured filter, scheduler, or test) ScmService quietly behaves as if the caller were org 1 instead of failing fast — masking bugs and risking cross-tenant reads/writes, while all sibling services in scope throw via TenantContext.requireOrganisationId().
findings.description: `private Long orgId() { Long id = TenantContext.getCurrentTenant(); return id != null ? id : 1L; }`. Every other service in the assigned set (ShariaService, RrpService, FraudService, OpResService, IaEngagementService, SanctionsScreeningService, SanctionsHitService) uses `TenantContext.requireOrganisationId()` which throws when the tenant is absent. ScmService instead silently falls back to organisation 1.
findings.rootCause: An early dev convenience (so the SCM UI worked before auth wiring was complete) was never removed; it predates the requireOrganisationId convention adopted by later modules.
findings.evidence: ScmService.java:39-42 returns 1L; contrast ShariaService.java:682 `static Long org() { return TenantContext.requireOrganisationId(); }` and OpResService.java:295 identical. ScmService is also the only in-scope module that performs NO audit.log/DomainEvent emission on any mutation — inconsistent with the F7/F8 convention every sibling follows.
findings.impact: If the tenant filter ever fails to populate context, SCM operations execute against tenant 1's vendors/contracts silently — a latent cross-tenant data-exposure path and a debugging trap, since reads succeed instead of 401/500.
findings.reproduction: Clear TenantContext and call ScmService.listVendors(): it returns org-1 vendors instead of throwing, unlike ShariaService.listScholars() which throws.
findings.resolution: Replace the 1L fallback with TenantContext.requireOrganisationId() to fail fast and match the platform convention. Separately, add the missing F7/F8 audit/event emission for SCM mutations for consistency (track as its own item).
references: CLAUDE.md: 'Every repository query must filter by organisation_id'

findings.title: Long, high-branching methods in ShariaService and IncidentService exceed the 40-LOC guideline
findings.cvss: Readability/testability risk: several single methods bundle querying, in-memory bucketing, builder assembly and side-effects, making them hard to unit-test in isolation and easy to break when a column is added.
findings.description: Measured method spans over the ~40-LOC guideline: ShariaService.dashboard() = 73 LOC with ~20 repository calls plus three in-place LinkedHashMap bucketing loops (561-633); ShariaService.transitionProduct() = 56 LOC switch with 7 cases each mutating different fields (496-551); IncidentService.regulatoryTemplates() = 57 LOC building 5 near-identical template maps (282-338); ThreeLinesService.overview() = ~73 LOC mixing role resolution, 4 register pulls, in-memory bucketing and a hard-coded 8-arg band() builder (111-183). transitionResolution (235-282, 48 LOC) and transitionCycle in RrpService are similar.
findings.rootCause: Dashboard/aggregation and transition-with-side-effect logic was kept inline rather than decomposed into per-section private helpers.
findings.evidence: awk LOC counts: ShariaService.dashboard 561-633 => 73; transitionProduct 496-551 => 56; IncidentService.regulatoryTemplates 282-338 => 57. ThreeLinesService.overview 111-183 => ~73 with the 8-positional-arg band() calls (160-167) that are themselves error-prone (all those bare 0 literals).
findings.impact: Each method is hard to read and test; the positional band(...) calls in ThreeLinesService (e.g. `band(LINE_1, roles, line1Risks, 0, line1Capa, 0, 0, line1Overdue, 0)`) are especially fragile — a transposed zero is a silent metric bug.
findings.reproduction: Open the cited ranges; count branches/statements. dashboard() has 3 loops + ~20 sequential repo calls in one method body.
findings.resolution: Extract per-section private helpers (e.g. resolutionStats(), findingStats(), productStats() for the dashboard; one renderTemplate-driven loop over a small template descriptor list for regulatoryTemplates) and replace the 8-positional-arg band() with a small builder/record to make the zeros self-documenting.

findings.title: IllegalTransitionException constructed with an empty allowed-set, discarding the real allowed transitions from the error message
findings.cvss: Diagnostics-quality smell: the transition exception is designed to carry the set of legal next states, but several call sites pass Set.of(), so the resulting 400 error tells the caller nothing about what would have been valid — degrading API ergonomics and support triage.
findings.description: AuditLifecycleService validates transitions with an inline `switch` returning a boolean and, on failure, throws `new IllegalTransitionException(from, to, Set.of())` (lines 104, 178, 250). The exception's third argument is meant to be the legal target set (cf. FindingService.java:115 and IaEngagementService.java:234 which pass the real `allowed` set). Because the allowed set was computed implicitly inside the switch and never materialised, an empty set is passed and the helpful 'allowed: [...]' detail is lost.
findings.rootCause: AuditLifecycleService uses a boolean-returning switch for transition validation instead of the Map<String,Set<String>> approach the other services use, so there is no allowed-set object to hand to the exception.
findings.evidence: AuditLifecycleService.java:104 `if (!ok) throw new IllegalTransitionException(from, to, Set.of());` (repeated at 178, 250). Compare FindingService.java:113-115 which builds `allowed` then throws `new IllegalTransitionException(f.getStatus(), req.getStatus(), allowed)`.
findings.impact: Clients/operators receive 'illegal transition X -> Y' with no hint of valid targets; inconsistent error payloads between audit_lc artefacts (AnnualPlan/WorkingPaper/CapaTask) and the rest of the platform.
findings.reproduction: POST an invalid AnnualPlan transition (e.g. DRAFT -> CLOSED): the IllegalTransitionException is raised with an empty allowed set, so the message omits the legal {AC_REVIEW}.
findings.resolution: Replace the boolean switches with the same `Map<String,Set<String>>` pattern (AP_ALLOWED/WP_ALLOWED/CAPA_ALLOWED) used elsewhere and pass the resolved set to the exception, restoring the informative message.
findings.patchAfter:
Set<String> allowed = AP_ALLOWED.getOrDefault(from, Set.of());
if (!allowed.contains(to)) throw new IllegalTransitionException(from, to, allowed);

findings.title: FraudService.closeCase reconstructs prior status from timestamps after overwriting it — fragile derivation with stale comment
findings.cvss: Correctness-fragility smell: the F8 event's priorStatus is guessed from outcome timestamps because the real prior status was already overwritten, producing values ('RESOLVED','OPEN') that are not even members of the case status vocabulary and can mislead downstream rules.
findings.description: closeCase() sets status to CLOSED at line 283, then at 295-301 emits FRAUD_CASE_CLOSED with `priorStatus` derived as `saved.getConfirmedLossSar() != null ? "CONFIRMED" : saved.getOutcomeSetAt() != null ? "RESOLVED" : "OPEN"`. The real prior status (CONFIRMED/CLEARED/FALSE_POSITIVE) was available before the overwrite but was not captured. The emitted strings 'RESOLVED' and 'OPEN' are not valid FraudCase statuses, so any rule matching on priorStatus equality will misfire.
findings.rootCause: The prior status was not saved into a local before `c.setStatus("CLOSED")`, forcing a lossy timestamp-based reconstruction (the inline comment admits 'we already overwrote it').
findings.evidence: Line 283 `c.setStatus("CLOSED")`; lines 297-300 reconstruct priorStatus from confirmedLossSar/outcomeSetAt yielding 'CONFIRMED'/'RESOLVED'/'OPEN'. ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS shows the only legal pre-CLOSED states are CONFIRMED, CLEARED, FALSE_POSITIVE — none of which is 'RESOLVED' or 'OPEN'.
findings.impact: Automation rules conditioning on the FRAUD_CASE_CLOSED priorStatus receive fabricated/incorrect values (CLEARED and FALSE_POSITIVE both collapse to 'RESOLVED'); breaks the F8 contract subtly.
findings.reproduction: Close a CLEARED case: the emitted priorStatus is 'RESOLVED', not 'CLEARED'.
findings.resolution: Capture `String prior = c.getStatus();` before setting CLOSED and emit the real value, mirroring how transitionResolution/transitionProduct capture `from` first.
